slides.say: The operation diamond is defined for every positive integer x. Diamond of x is three x when x is odd, and x squared minus twelve when x is even. Given: diamond of x is equal to twenty-four. x is equal to what?

This time it's backwards. They give us the result, twenty-four, and we need the input. And we don't know if x is odd or even. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, trying both rules, and then plugging in the answers.

[short pause] Let's try both rules. First the odd rule. Three x is twenty-four, so x is twenty-four divided by three, which is eight. But wait. Eight is even, and an even number never uses the odd rule. So eight doesn't fit the rule it came from, and we throw it out.
Now the even rule. x squared minus twelve is twenty-four. Add twelve to both sides, so x squared is thirty-six. x is positive, so x is six. And six is even, so it really uses the even rule. It fits.
So x is six, and choice number two is our answer. Choice numbers one and three keep the eight, which came from the wrong rule.
at: choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now let's plug in the answers. Each choice tells us x, so we first check if it's odd or even, and then use the right rule. Choice number one is eight. Eight is even, so the even rule. Eight squared is sixty-four, and sixty-four minus twelve is fifty-two. That's not twenty-four, so eight is out.
Choice number two is six. Six is even, so again the even rule. Six squared is thirty-six, and thirty-six minus twelve is twenty-four. It works.

Choice number three says six or eight, so it claims that both values work. Eight doesn't work, so the whole choice is wrong, even though six works. And six works, so choice number four, no such x, is out. Choice number two is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Choice number two is our answer
